item.title: Santa Rosa County cancels Veterans Day Parade, plans ceremony at memorial
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Santa Rosa County Veterans Memorial Foundation has decided to cancel this year's Veterans Day Parade as the community continues cleanup and recovery following Hurricane Isaias, but organizers say the commitment to honoring veterans remains unchanged. Instead of the parade, the foundation is inviting the public to a Veterans Day Ceremony and…
item.content:encoded:
The Santa Rosa County Veterans Memorial Foundation has decided to cancel this year's Veterans Day Parade as the community continues cleanup and recovery following Hurricane Isaias, but organizers say the commitment to honoring veterans remains unchanged.

Instead of the parade, the foundation is inviting the public to a Veterans Day Ceremony and wreath-laying at the Santa Rosa County Veterans Memorial on November 11 at 11 a.m., weather permitting. Foundation President Tom Powers said in a statement that "our community's safety and recovery must come first."

Following the ceremony, attendees are invited to gather at American Legion Post #78 in Milton for a Flag Retirement ceremony, bonfire, and cookout. Grover's Restaurant is donating food, which will be served by local Santa Rosa County 4-H Club members and volunteers. "Now, more than ever, this is a time for our community to come together, honor our veterans, lend a helping hand, and support one another as we continue to recover and rebuild," Powers said.

item.title: Taddeo Pledges Insurance Accountability Plan in Pensacola Roundtable
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Democratic candidate for Florida Chief Financial Officer Annette Taddeo held a roundtable discussion in Pensacola on Monday to address the state's ongoing insurance crisis, fielding concerns from residents about rising homeowners insurance costs and calling for stronger consumer protections. Taddeo, a former state senator, pledged to release a…
item.content:encoded:
Democratic candidate for Florida Chief Financial Officer Annette Taddeo held a roundtable discussion in Pensacola on Monday to address the state's ongoing insurance crisis, fielding concerns from residents about rising homeowners insurance costs and calling for stronger consumer protections.

Taddeo, a former state senator, pledged to release a report card evaluating insurance companies' financial stability within her first 100 days in office if elected. She also highlighted her previous legislative work pushing for greater transparency around insurers' affiliated companies, arguing that Florida needs an independent watchdog willing to hold the industry accountable regardless of political affiliation.

Joining the discussion was Dr. Frank Collige, a former Republican CFO primary candidate who has since backed Taddeo's campaign. Collige criticized the Department of Financial Services for failing to adequately police insurers when they violate the law, and pointed out that the CFO's office has conducted zero audits of insurance companies. "We need a CFO who will actually do audits, who will actually hold people accountable," Collige said.

Insurance expert Gary Rosen, Ph.D., also participated in the roundtable. Taddeo's campaign centers on three priorities: affordability, accountability, and anti-corruption. More information on her candidacy is available at annettetaddeo.com.

item.title: Senator Moody pushes cybersecurity bills targeting scams, child predators
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Senator Ashley Moody is using National Cybersecurity Month to spotlight her legislative efforts aimed at protecting Floridians from online threats, including child predators, scammers targeting seniors, and fraudulent schemes. Moody is championing several bipartisan measures. The Kids Online Safety Act, which she's supported since her time as…
item.content:encoded:
Senator Ashley Moody is using National Cybersecurity Month to spotlight her legislative efforts aimed at protecting Floridians from online threats, including child predators, scammers targeting seniors, and fraudulent schemes.

Moody is championing several bipartisan measures. The Kids Online Safety Act, which she's supported since her time as Florida's Attorney General, would give young people and parents tools and safeguards against online harms. She also introduced the STOP Scams Against Seniors Act to help law enforcement investigate and prosecute criminals who target older Floridians through financial fraud. Additionally, Moody is an original cosponsor of the No FAKES Act, legislation to protect Americans from having their voice and image stolen for unauthorized AI-generated deepfakes; that bill advanced out of the Senate Judiciary Committee in June.

Senator Moody also introduced the SWIPES Act to give law enforcement stronger tools to prosecute gift card fraud and impose tougher penalties on those who knowingly target seniors. Fraudsters often set up fake websites mimicking legitimate sites where consumers check gift card balances, then steal funds when victims enter their card information.

During her tenure as Florida Attorney General, Moody created the Cyber Fraud Enforcement Unit in 2023. According to her office, the unit froze more than $17 million in illicit funds tied to cryptocurrency scams and managed 40 active crypto seizure cases involving senior victims.

item.title: Mediacom Says More Than 90% of Hurricane Isaias Outages Restored
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: MILTON, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Mediacom says more than 90% of customers who lost service during Hurricane Isaias have been reconnected, but restoration work continues in some of Northwest Florida's hardest-hit communities. The company says Milton and surrounding areas remain a particular focus as crews work through more extensive damage. Mediacom…
item.content:encoded:
MILTON, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Mediacom says more than 90% of customers who lost service during Hurricane Isaias have been reconnected, but restoration work continues in some of Northwest Florida's hardest-hit communities.

The company says Milton and surrounding areas remain a particular focus as crews work through more extensive damage.

Mediacom says some locations require additional infrastructure repairs before customers can be reconnected.

Crews are continuing restoration work this week.

Customers still without service can check an individual estimated repair time through Mediacom's online outage map or MobileCARE app.

The company is also operating a free Wi-Fi trailer near Sonny's BBQ at 5129 Highway 90 in Pace.

The trailer is available from 8 a.m. until 8 p.m.

Mediacom has also temporarily opened community Wi-Fi hotspots for complimentary use across Florida, Alabama, Georgia and Mississippi.

Mediacom Mobile customers affected by the hurricane are receiving temporary data enhancements at no additional cost.

The company's restoration continues more than two weeks after Isaias caused widespread power, cable and communications damage across Northwest Florida.

item.title: Gulf Breeze Will Do Names 10 Finalists for 2026 Community Grants
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Gulf Breeze Will Do, a women's philanthropic organization, has selected 10 finalists for its 2026 grant awards from 18 applications requesting a combined $112,229.27. The finalists are requesting $52,260.35 total, though the organization has $44,600 available to distribute, according to a news release from the group. The finalist projects span…
item.content:encoded:
Gulf Breeze Will Do, a women's philanthropic organization, has selected 10 finalists for its 2026 grant awards from 18 applications requesting a combined $112,229.27. The finalists are requesting $52,260.35 total, though the organization has $44,600 available to distribute, according to a news release from the group.

The finalist projects span four categories: Art, Recreation & Sports; Education; Hardship Support Services; and Public Safety. Standout requests include a $10,000 grant for Gulf Breeze Middle School's "Protecting Every Heart" program, a $9,904.65 request from Soundside High School's ESE Department for a poster and banner production program, and a $9,708.59 proposal from Midway Fire District for firefighter thermal imaging equipment.

Other finalists include the Gulf Breeze Middle School Band seeking $6,534.98 for a touring support program, Gulf Breeze Elementary's project to replace outdoor water fountains ($2,843.99), and the Santa Rosa Education Foundation's Take Stock In Children laptop and backpack program ($2,902.47). Members of Gulf Breeze Will Do will vote on which projects receive funding at the organization's Annual Meeting on November 8 at 2 p.m. at the Gulf Breeze Recreation Center.

The organization, which serves Gulf Breeze and Pensacola Beach communities, operates on a model where 100 percent of annual $250 membership dues are awarded back to the community as grants. Every member votes to determine which organizations receive funding.

item.content:encoded:
A Fort Walton Beach man with a prior felony conviction has pleaded guilty to federal charges of cocaine trafficking and illegal firearm possession, according to WKRG News 5.

The case highlights ongoing drug enforcement efforts in the Panhandle region. Federal prosecutors typically pursue such cases when trafficking quantities and prior criminal history are involved, which can result in significantly enhanced sentences compared to state-level drug charges.

Details on the specific amount of cocaine, the firearm involved, or sentencing recommendations were not immediately available. The case will proceed to sentencing, where a federal judge will determine the consequences of the guilty pleas.

item.title: Northwest Florida Still Waiting for FEMA Assistance as Recovery Enters Third Week
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Northwest Florida is entering its third week of Hurricane Isaias recovery without federal approval that would allow storm victims to apply for FEMA Individual Assistance. Florida has requested a Major Disaster Declaration covering communities affected by the Oct. 9 hurricane. The request seeks Individual…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Northwest Florida is entering its third week of Hurricane Isaias recovery without federal approval that would allow storm victims to apply for FEMA Individual Assistance.

Florida has requested a Major Disaster Declaration covering communities affected by the Oct. 9 hurricane.

The request seeks Individual Assistance for qualifying residents in eight Northwest Florida counties, including Escambia and Santa Rosa.

It also seeks Public Assistance for 15 counties to help governments recover eligible costs for debris removal, emergency work and damaged public infrastructure.

As of Monday morning, the request remained under federal review.

Congressman Jimmy Patronis told NewsRadio 92.3 Monday that he has been communicating with the Trump administration about the request.

Patronis said Florida's congressional delegation, including Senators Ashley Moody and Rick Scott, has been pressing the administration for action.

He said he may have an opportunity to speak directly with President Donald Trump about the request Friday.

Until a Major Disaster Declaration authorizing Individual Assistance is approved, Hurricane Isaias victims cannot apply to FEMA for that program.

Local damage estimates continue mounting.

Santa Rosa County reports more than 100 structures destroyed, more than 400 with major damage and thousands more affected.

Pensacola estimates $71.7 million in private-property damage inside city limits, while Milton says as many as 60% of structures there suffered some level of damage.

Local and state recovery programs continue operating while the federal request is considered.

item.title: 15-Year-Old Arrested in FAMU Homecoming Shooting That Injured 12
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: TALLAHASSEE, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- A 15-year-old has been arrested on 11 counts of attempted second-degree murder following a shooting that injured a dozen people during Florida A&M University's homecoming weekend. Tallahassee Police identified the suspect as Anthony Rivers III. Investigators say a physical altercation involving people who knew…
item.content:encoded:
TALLAHASSEE, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- A 15-year-old has been arrested on 11 counts of attempted second-degree murder following a shooting that injured a dozen people during Florida A&M University's homecoming weekend.

Tallahassee Police identified the suspect as Anthony Rivers III.

Investigators say a physical altercation involving people who knew each other preceded the gunfire Saturday night near Perry and Manatee streets, close to FAMU's campus.

Eleven people were struck by gunfire.

Another person suffered an ankle injury while trying to escape.

Six of the victims are adults and six are juveniles.

Three suffered serious injuries, while the others were initially reported in stable condition.

Police say their investigation indicates none of the people who were injured were intentionally targeted.

Rivers is also charged with possession of a firearm by a delinquent.

The investigation remains active, and Tallahassee Police say additional arrests are possible.

Drivers and residents in affected areas should watch for construction activity and exercise caution around work zones.

item.title: Santa Rosa County celebrates agriculture at Rural Roots Day Ag Expo in Jay

The family-friendly event aims to celebrate the agricultural heritage and rural traditions that have shaped the county's farming communities. The all-day expo will feature free food, educational…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County is hosting its second annual Rural Roots Day on Saturday, November 14, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. at the UF/IFAS Research Center in Jay. The family-friendly event aims to celebrate the agricultural heritage and rural traditions that have shaped the county's farming communities.

The all-day expo will feature free food, educational activities, and hands-on experiences for visitors of all ages. Highlights include a Fall Heritage Pie Contest, live animals, a hay maze, kids' crafts, a planting station, and panel discussions with local farmers about farming traditions and agricultural practices.

The event is organized by Santa Rosa County, UF/IFAS Extension's West Florida Research and Education Center, the Santa Rosa County Fair Association, and Santa Rosa County 4-H. More details and information about entering the Fall Heritage Pie Contest are available at www.santarosa.fl.gov/RuralRootsDay.

item.title: Three NAS Pensacola Sailors Killed in Fiery Weekend Crash
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Three people killed in a fiery crash in Pensacola early Saturday morning were all U.S. Navy sailors stationed at NAS Pensacola. The single-vehicle crash happened around 1:35 a.m. near Cervantes and M streets. The vehicle struck a barrier and caught fire, killing all three occupants. The Navy says two of the…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Three people killed in a fiery crash in Pensacola early Saturday morning were all U.S. Navy sailors stationed at NAS Pensacola.

The single-vehicle crash happened around 1:35 a.m. near Cervantes and M streets.

The vehicle struck a barrier and caught fire, killing all three occupants.

The Navy says two of the sailors were assigned to the Naval Air Technical Training Center at NAS Pensacola. One held the rank of E-1 and the other was an E-2.

The third sailor was an E-2 assigned to Naval Aviation Schools Command.

The sailors' names had not been publicly released pending notification of their families.

Naval Education and Training Command said grief counseling and support are being made available to family members, friends and fellow sailors through Navy chaplains and other resources.

Pensacola Police continue investigating the crash.

Initial reports differed on the direction the vehicle was traveling before impact, and police have not publicly announced a cause.

The crash was one of several serious incidents investigated across the Pensacola area over the weekend.

item.title: UWF tapped to lead South Regional Hub for national cybersecurity education assessment
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The University of West Florida's Center for Cybersecurity and AI has been selected to lead the South Regional Hub for a new national effort to measure how cybersecurity education translates into workforce development and economic benefit. The initiative, called the Economic Assessment National Center, or EANC, is funded through a roughly $1.5…
item.content:encoded:
The University of West Florida's Center for Cybersecurity and AI has been selected to lead the South Regional Hub for a new national effort to measure how cybersecurity education translates into workforce development and economic benefit.

The initiative, called the Economic Assessment National Center, or EANC, is funded through a roughly $1.5 million, two-year award from the National Security Agency's National Centers of Academic Excellence in Cybersecurity program. UWF will work alongside six other regional hubs across the country — led nationally by Coastline College in California — to develop a consistent framework for measuring the impact of cybersecurity education on workforce readiness, economic growth, and national security priorities.

Dr. Eman El-Sheikh, UWF's associate vice president for the Center for Cybersecurity and AI, said the center will connect with cybersecurity-designated institutions across the South, facilitate collaboration, and help build measurement tools that show how education translates to real-world outcomes. "This initiative will help us better measure, communicate and amplify the collective impact of cybersecurity education on workforce readiness, economic growth and national security," El-Sheikh said.

UWF brings significant expertise to the role. The center previously served as the Southeast CAE Regional Hub from 2017 to 2022 and currently leads the National Cybersecurity Workforce Development Program. The new EANC will develop a Performance Measurement Framework that tracks graduate outcomes, industry certifications, workforce pathways, and economic contributions, then produce national reports and data dashboards to help institutions and federal agencies understand the broader value of cybersecurity education.

item.content:encoded:
Drivers crossing Escambia and Santa Rosa counties should expect construction-related delays this week as maintenance crews tackle several state road projects.

The Florida Department of Transportation says work is underway on Interstate 10 with resurfacing operations east of U.S. 231, along with activity on other state routes throughout the region. The agency typically posts weekly construction notices to alert commuters to potential slowdowns during peak travel times.

Motorists are advised to allow extra time for trips and watch for work zone signs. For real-time traffic updates and detailed project information, drivers can check the FDOT website or local traffic reports before heading out.

item.title: IMPACT 100 distributes record $1.313M to 13 nonprofits across Escambia, Santa Rosa counties

The grants were announced during the organization's Annual Meeting, reflecting the 23rd consecutive year that IMPACT 100 has distributed funds to nonprofits serving…
item.content:encoded:
IMPACT 100 Pensacola Bay Area announced Sunday that it has awarded $101,000 grants to 13 local nonprofit organizations, marking a record $1.313 million in total giving for the year. The grants were announced during the organization's Annual Meeting, reflecting the 23rd consecutive year that IMPACT 100 has distributed funds to nonprofits serving Escambia and Santa Rosa counties.

The funding represents a significant boost for local charitable work across the region. IMPACT 100's grant program operates through a membership-driven model where donors pool contributions to support vetted nonprofit organizations working in education, health, social services, and community development.

The specific nonprofits receiving this year's awards were not immediately detailed in the announcement, though the $1.313 million total underscores growing community support for organized philanthropy in Northwest Florida.

item.title: Century Town Clerk Moore Earns State Professional Certification
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Carrie Moore, town clerk for the Town of Century, has earned her Florida Certified Professional Clerk (FCPC) designation, a credential conferred by the John Scott Dailey Florida Institute of Government at Florida State University in partnership with the Florida Association of City Clerks. The FCPC designation recognizes professional competency and…
item.content:encoded:
Carrie Moore, town clerk for the Town of Century, has earned her Florida Certified Professional Clerk (FCPC) designation, a credential conferred by the John Scott Dailey Florida Institute of Government at Florida State University in partnership with the Florida Association of City Clerks.

The FCPC designation recognizes professional competency and expertise in municipal clerk duties and administration. Moore's achievement reflects her commitment to professional development in local government service.

Century, located in north Escambia County, is one of the area's smaller municipalities. The certification underscores the importance local government places on ensuring clerks maintain current knowledge of state law, municipal operations, and best practices in public administration.
